briefdescription.para: Collect the instructions that are uniform after vectorization.

detaileddescription.para: An instruction is uniform if we represent it with a single scalar value in the vectorized loop corresponding to each vector iteration. Examples of uniform instructions include pointer operands of consecutive or interleaved memory accesses. Note that although uniformity implies an instruction will be scalar, the reverse is not true. In general, a scalarized instruction will be represented by VF scalar values in the vectorized loop, each corresponding to an iteration of the original scalar loop.

briefdescription.para: Collect the instructions that are scalar after vectorization.

detaileddescription.para: An instruction is scalar if it is known to be uniform or will be scalarized during vectorization. collectLoopScalars should only add non-uniform nodes to the list if they are used by a load/store instruction that is marked as CM_Scalarize. Non-uniform scalarized instructions will be represented by VF values in the vectorized loop, each corresponding to an iteration of the original scalar loop.
